title: Criteria and Guidelines for Returning to Running Following a Tibial Bone Stress Injury: A Scoping Review
authors: George E, Sheerin K, Reid D
population: 50 studies (39 reviews or clinical commentaries, 3 retrospective cohorts, 2 RCTs, 2 pilot studies, 1 prospective observational study, 3 case studies) on returning to running after tibial BSI
findings: Fifty studies were included; recommendations rest on level IV evidence.

Five components should be addressed before introducing running: resolution of bony tenderness, pain-free walking, radiological healing evidence in high-risk BSIs, strength, functional and loading tests, and identification of contributing factors.
An individualised graduated programme should be started, often with walk-run intervals, progressing running distance ahead of speed and intensity, with symptom provocation a key consideration.
Return-to-run decisions should be shared between clinician, coach and athlete; contributing factors to the initial injury should be addressed throughout.
limitations: Scoping review (classified here as systematic-review design for lack of a closer category); evidence is level IV, mostly expert opinion; tibial BSI only; the abstract gives no interval durations or distances.
implications: Gate the return-to-run plan on athlete-confirmed criteria (no bony tenderness, pain-free walking, clinician clearance when high-risk) before generating any running.

Start with walk-run intervals and increase running distance before pace or intensity; hold progression when symptoms recur. Interval durations are not in the evidence; use conservative defaults and label them grade D.
